text:
raj: Heads up - noticed two customers with duplicate SCIM users after last KMS alias swap. Not a full outage but bad for audits.

toni: Duplicates how? Both have same email/displayName or slight differences?

raj: Exact same email/displayName. One user row has extId starting with "jwe:v1:" and the other with "jwe:v2:". SCIM flow tried POST -> 201 then another POST -> 409 then we created second account on retry.

lina: Can you paste the provisioning log?

raj: Snip: ```
2026-03-21T04:02:03Z INFO scim-provisioner tenant=org-77 request=POST /Users -> 201 id=usr_liveA
2026-03-21T04:02:04Z INFO scim-provisioner reconcile found externalId decrypt failed -> null
2026-03-21T04:02:04Z INFO scim-provisioner attempt=2 POST /Users -> 409 Conflict {"detail":"externalId mismatch"}
2026-03-21T04:02:05Z INFO scim-provisioner reconcile create fallback id=usr_shadowB
2026-03-21T04:02:06Z ERROR kms-client decrypt failed alg=RSA-OAEP reason="unsupported alg header"
```

toni: Looks like some extIds are still wrapped with the old OAEP header. We rotated alias + kicked off a rewrap, but some tenants with heavy provisioning windows failed.

lina: If we create shadow accounts we risk splitting RBAC. Downstream entitlement keys use extId as canonical key. We need a safe merge path.

raj: Proposed immediate plan: 1) Add transient decryption fallback in scim-provisioner to try both legacy and current algs when reading extId. If fallback succeeds, rewrap to new alias and update record atomically. 2) If decrypt fails, do NOT create a shadow account; instead enqueue a reconcile-deferred job and mark the provisioning event in audit stream.

toni: For merges: create a transactional merge job that finds candidate pairs (same email) and does: copy role bindings from shadow -> canonical, reassign service principals, delete shadow, emit audit record with old_extid/new_extid/roles/actor. All in one DB tx.

lina: We should also build a dry-run that reports what will change per-tenant so security/compliance can review before merging for sensitive tenants.

raj: Agreed. I'll also add a one-off backfill script to rewrap extIds using fallback decrypt and record successes/failures. Backfill will not auto-merge; it will flag candidates for the transactional merge tool.

audit-bot: Note: rotation idp-encrypt-prod -> idp-encrypt-v2; rewrap job ran 2026-03-21T01:10:00Z; failures=12 tenants.

toni: Action items:
- raj: implement decrypt-fallback + enqueue-defer (ETA 3h)
- lina: design transactional merge tool + dry-run report (ETA 6h)
- security: run dry-run on the 12 failed tenants and sign off for merge (ETA 24h)
- infra-bot: add alert if scim-provisioner creates >0 shadow accounts in any tenant in 30m window (page eng-sre)

lina: Also add audit entries for any extId rewrap or merge with fields: timestamp, tenant, actor=system, before_extid, after_extid, merged_user_ids, roles_migrated. Compliance needs this for reconciliation.

raj: One extra edge: service accounts with long-running sessions may have extIds cached in downstream systems. When we rewrap extId we should retain a short-lived compatibility mapping for 7 days to avoid auth breaks. Will include in backfill plan.

toni: Good. After we have dry-run results we'll coordinate customer comms for the ones where merge is non-trivial.

raj: Kicking off work now, will paste results here.

lina: Thanks — I'll open a tracking ticket and attach the dry-run template.

raj: Initial quick check shows 8 tenants with straight-forward merges, 4 need manual review.

audit-bot: Audit note created: audit/SCIM_REWRAP_RUN/1768923456 - 2026-03-21T04:05:00Z - initiator=raj - flagged=12 - dry_run_id=dr_20260321_01

toni: Perfect. keep this channel updated.
